data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms not as an inductive inference to truth or probability, but as a non-inductive methodological rule grounded in the aim of science: maximizing verisimilitude (truth-likeness) through severe testing. The 'cost' of accepting this defense is the abandonment of any guarantee that the preferred theory is true or even probable, requiring scientists to act on a critical rational faith that the unrefuted theory is closer to the truth than its refuted rivals, without empirical proof that past success predicts future reliability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If corroboration is strictly a historical report with no bearing on future performance, then preferring Theory A over Theory B becomes an arbitrary act indistinguishable from induction, violating Popper's demand for a logical distinction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the concept of verisimilitude is logically incoherent (as Tich\u00fd and Miller argued), then the entire defense collapses because there is no coherent 'aim' (getting closer to truth) that corroboration allegedly serves.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If acting on a theory implies an expectation of its practical success, then Popper smuggles in pragmatic induction under the guise of 'methodological rules,' failing to escape the problem of induction entirely.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism distinguishes between 'justification of belief' (which Popper rejects as inductive) and 'rationality of action' (which he accepts as critical). Preference is justified by the logical asymmetry of falsification: while corroboration cannot increase probability, it indicates that a theory has withstood attempts to falsify it where others have failed. Acting on the best-tested theory is the only rational strategy if one's goal is to approximate truth, because choosing a falsified or less-tested theory would be knowingly acting on inferior information. This avoids induction by treating corroboration as a report of past performance, not a predictor of future success, yet acknowledging it as the sole guide available to a fallibilist.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
